scenario: Elevate Health 的第三方猎头电话：他开场就把你现在的公司说成 AWS，通话内容很薄。这已经是你连续第六次走到「你有什么想问我的」。
scenario_en: A third-party headhunter call for Elevate Health: he opened by saying you work at AWS, and the call was thin. This is the sixth interview in a row reaching "any questions for me?"
q: 通话质量这么差，准备好的两个问题还问吗？
q_en: The call was low quality — do you still ask the two questions you prepared?
options: 算了——通话本来就很水、对方连你在哪家公司都搞错了，礼貌说一句没有问题，把时间还给他。
照样问出纸上那两个问题，并用其中一个顺手纠正背景：我现在在 TikTok，不是 AWS。
只问「后面还有几轮、大概什么时候出结果」，把这通电话当成纯流程沟通处理掉。
当场即兴想一个泛问题，比如「你们公司文化怎么样」，凑满反问环节，不至于冷场。
options_en: Skip it — the call was sloppy and he didn't even know which company you work at, so politely say you have no questions and give him the time back.
Ask both questions from the paper anyway, and use one of them to fix the background: I'm at TikTok, not AWS.
Only ask "how many rounds are left and when will I hear back," treating the call as pure logistics.
Improvise a generic question like "what's the culture like here" just to fill the slot and avoid silence.
tradeoff: 照常问 vs 因通话质量放弃：放弃省下三分钟，代价是第六次留下「没问题」的记录，而且我依然没有任何判断这家公司的信息。
why: 连续六次没问实质问题已经是记录在案的模式，通话差不是豁免：这是我唯一能主动拿信息、也是唯一能纠正他弄错背景的窗口。
why_en: Six calls with no real questions is a documented pattern, and a sloppy call is no excuse — this is my only window to pull information and to fix what he got wrong about me.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方明确说时间到了、必须立刻挂断时，才该压缩成一个问题，并说明剩下的会邮件补问。
optionMeanings: 放弃反问，把时间还给对方。
照问两问，其中一问兼做背景纠正。
只问轮次和出结果时间。
临场抛一个通用文化问题。
optionMeanings_en: Give up the slot and hand the time back.
Ask both, using one to correct the background.
Ask only about rounds and timeline.
Improvise a generic culture question.
optionDirectness: 只有对方已宣布挂断时才成立；这里是主动关掉唯一的信息窗口。
猎头搞错背景时，纠正和提问可以合成一句，不必单独争辩。
轮次与时间线适合会后邮件问，占掉现场名额就浪费了。
泛文化题换谁问都是同一句，得到的回答也一样空。
optionDirectness_en: Only right if they already said the call must end; here it closes the one information window.
When a headhunter has your background wrong, the correction and the question can be one sentence.
Rounds and timing belong in a follow-up email; spending a live slot on them wastes it.
A generic culture question sounds the same from any candidate and gets an equally empty answer.
optionScenarioImpacts: 第六次「无问题」进记录，模式坐实。
既拿到判断这家的信息，也把 AWS 的错纠回来。
他会认定我只关心能不能过，不关心这份工作。
听完回答我还是不知道这家值不值得投。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A sixth "no questions" goes on the record and the pattern hardens.
You get real information and repair the AWS mistake at the same time.
He concludes you only care about passing, not about the job.
After the answer you still can't tell whether this company is worth pursuing.

q: 面试流程类问题该问谁、在哪问？现场那两个名额留给什么？
q_en: Who do you ask process questions, and where — and what are the two live slots reserved for?
text: 流程问题（还有几轮、何时出结果、下一轮谁面）归{{招聘人}}，而且可以放到{{会后邮件}}里问；现场那两个提问名额只留给关于{{这份工作本身}}的问题。
text_en: Process questions — rounds left, timeline, who's next — belong to the {{recruiter}} and can go in a {{follow-up email}}; the two live slots are only for questions about {{the work itself}}.
why: 只问流程等于用掉了唯一一次提问机会，却没问关于这份工作的任何事——听上去像我只关心能不能过，不关心进来做什么。
why_en: Asking only about process burns my one chance without asking anything about the job, which reads as caring about passing rather than about the work.

scenario: 为了终结「连续六次没有实质反问」的模式，你要把反问变成一个固定动作，而不是临场发挥。
scenario_en: To end the "six interviews with no real questions" pattern, you want asking questions to be a fixed ritual, not improvisation.
q: 把反问的固定动作排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four steps of the questions ritual in the right order.
steps: 收尾时先问纸上那两个，再问现场长出来的那一个
会前按公司类型选一组：Applied AI / 早期创业 / B2B SaaS / 通用兜底
通话中随手记下他提到的一个具体事实，用它长出第三个问题
从这一组里挑两个写在纸上，放在屏幕旁边
why: 问题不是临场想出来的：会前按公司类型选组、挑两个写在纸上，通话中再补一个从他话里长出来的，收尾时三个都有着落。
why_en: Questions don't get invented on the spot — pick a set by company type, put two on paper, and grow a third from something they actually said.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["会前 5 分钟"] --> B["按公司类型选一组"]
  B --> C["挑 2 个写在纸上"]
  C --> D["通话中记 1 个现场事实"]
  D --> E["收尾: 先纸上 后现场"]

scenario: 面 Assembled / Anytime AI / Daisy 这类 applied AI 公司：产品核心是让 AI agent 替客户处理工单。你有两个提问名额。
scenario_en: You're interviewing at an applied-AI company like Assembled, Anytime AI, or Daisy, where the product is an AI agent handling customer tickets. You have two question slots.
q: 这一类公司该问哪一组问题？
q_en: Which set of questions fits this kind of company?
options: 让 agent 可靠到客户敢不派人工兜底，最难的是哪一块？
你们后端主要用什么语言和框架？跑在 AWS 上还是自建集群？
公司现在多少人、融到第几轮？接下来准备扩到多大规模？
你们这个方向前景怎么样？AI 现在很火，未来两三年产品打算往哪走？
options_en: What's the hardest part of making the agent reliable enough that customers stop keeping a human on standby?
What language and framework is your backend? Do you run on AWS or your own cluster?
How many people are you now, and which round have you raised? How big are you planning to grow?
How's the outlook for this space? AI is hot right now — where does the product go in two or three years?
tradeoff: 问可靠性 vs 问技术栈：技术栈问题谁都能问、答案还写在 JD 里，代价是我完全没碰到这家在 AI 上真正的难处。
why: applied AI 公司真正的难处是 agent 的可靠性和评估方式，问这个才说明我懂这个品类；技术栈的答案 JD 上就有。
why_en: For an applied-AI company the real pain is agent reliability and how they evaluate it, so asking that shows I understand the category — the stack is already in the job description.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮的面试官是招聘人而不是工程师，把它换成「团队怎么判断一条 agent 回复算好」，更容易拿到实质回答。
optionMeanings: 问 agent 可靠性的真实瓶颈。
问语言、框架与部署环境。
问人数与融资阶段。
问赛道前景与产品远期规划。
optionMeanings_en: Ask where agent reliability actually breaks.
Ask about language, framework, and hosting.
Ask about headcount and funding stage.
Ask about market outlook and long-range roadmap.
optionDirectness: 可靠性是这个品类唯一决定客户续不续约的东西。
属于 JD 已经写明的信息，问了不增加任何判断。
适合 pre-seed 的尽调场合，这里公司阶段已经清楚。
远期规划连创始人也只能给方向，答案无法验证。
optionDirectness_en: Reliability is the one thing that decides whether these customers renew.
This is already spelled out in the job description, so it adds no judgment.
Fits a pre-seed diligence call; here the company stage is already known.
Even founders can only gesture at long-range plans, so the answer can't be checked.
optionScenarioImpacts: 他会开始讲真实的失败案例，我立刻听出团队成熟度。
得到一份技术清单，对是否加入没有帮助。
像在做背调，不像在关心他们的产品难题。
换来一段愿景陈述，任何公司都能给同样的话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: He starts describing real failure cases and you immediately read the team's maturity.
You get a list of technologies that doesn't help you decide anything.
It sounds like background checking rather than caring about their product problem.
You get a vision statement any company could have given.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自己调用工具、多步完成一件事的 LLM 系统，这里指替客服处理工单的那种。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AI agent is an LLM system that calls tools and takes multiple steps on its own, here one that resolves support tickets.

scenario: GenLogs 这类 100 人以下的早期创业公司 recruiter screen：产品刚有第一批客户，工程团队还在搭。
scenario_en: A recruiter screen at an early-stage startup under 100 people like GenLogs: first customers just landed and the engineering team is still being built.
q: 这通电话该问哪两个问题？
q_en: Which two questions belong in this call?
options: 公司有没有 401k 匹配、几天年假、能不能远程办公？
面试一共几轮、下一轮是谁面、大概多久能出结果？
这个岗位入职 90 天什么算成功？团队现在最大的、还没定的技术决策是什么？
你们技术栈是什么？前端用 React 吗？数据库是 Postgres 还是 MongoDB？CI 用什么？
options_en: Do you match 401k, how much vacation, and is remote allowed?
How many rounds are there, who's next, and how long until I hear back?
What does success look like in the first 90 days? What's the biggest technical decision still open?
What's your stack? React on the front end? Postgres or MongoDB? What do you use for CI?
tradeoff: 问 90 天与未定决策 vs 问福利与技术栈：后者答案确定、好问，代价是问不出这家团队现在真正卡在哪。
why: 早期公司最有信息量的两件事是「他们对这个岗位的期待」和「哪个决策还没定」；后者的答案直接告诉我进去第一个月要干什么。
why_en: At an early-stage company the two most informative things are what they expect from this hire and which decision is still open, and the second one tells me what my first month looks like.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮的招聘人只做前置筛选、明显答不了技术问题，就把未定决策那题留给下一轮的工程师。
optionMeanings: 问福利、假期与远程政策。
问轮次、面试官与时间线。
问 90 天期待与未定的技术决策。
问语言、框架、数据库与 CI。
optionMeanings_en: Ask about benefits, vacation, and remote policy.
Ask about rounds, interviewers, and timeline.
Ask about 90-day expectations and the open technical decision.
Ask about language, framework, database, and CI.
optionDirectness: 这些等到 offer 阶段由招聘人一次给全，现在问是浪费名额。
邮件里问同样能拿到，占用现场时间没有额外收益。
两问分别拿到「他们要什么」和「团队卡在哪」。
清单式技术问题在 JD 或 LinkedIn 上就能查到。
optionDirectness_en: The recruiter hands all of this over at offer stage, so spending a slot now wastes it.
An email gets the same answer, so live time on it buys nothing extra.
The two together give you what they want and where the team is stuck.
A checklist of technologies is already findable in the posting or on LinkedIn.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场就聊待遇，会被读成对工作本身没兴趣。
第六次只谈流程，「不好奇」的印象再加一层。
他会说出团队真实的痛点，我能判断要不要继续。
拿到一串名词，对这家值不值得去毫无帮助。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Leading with compensation reads as no interest in the work itself.
A sixth process-only round adds another layer to the "not curious" impression.
He names the team's real pain and you can decide whether to continue.
You collect a list of nouns that tells you nothing about whether to join.

scenario: Pinpoint Global 是 15 人的金融合规 workflow 公司：客户是受监管机构，产品有大量按客户定制的流程。
scenario_en: Pinpoint Global is a 15-person financial-compliance workflow company: regulated clients, and a lot of the product is customized per client.
q: 这类 B2B SaaS 公司该问什么才问到点上？
q_en: What actually hits the mark at this kind of B2B SaaS company?
options: 新功能开发和给现有客户做定制维护各占多少？工程师参与客户早期对话吗？
合规行业是不是特别看重稳定？你们平时加班多不多、节奏怎么样？
你们打算什么时候上 AI？我觉得大模型在合规场景应该很有用，有没有在做？
团队现在多少人？我看官网写 15 人左右，是不是还在快速招人？
options_en: How much of the work is new features versus customizing and maintaining for existing clients? Do engineers join early customer conversations?
Does compliance mean stability matters more? How much overtime is there, what's the pace like?
When are you adding AI? Large models seem useful for compliance — is anything in progress?
How big is the team? The site says around 15 — are you still hiring fast?
tradeoff: 问新功能与定制的比例 vs 问节奏和 AI 计划：后者容易开口，代价是问不出我每天到底会写什么代码。
why: 定制型 B2B 公司里，新功能与客户定制的比例直接决定我每天的工作长什么样；这个比例招聘人答得出，官网上却查不到。
why_en: At a customization-heavy B2B company the split between new features and client-specific work decides what my day actually looks like, and only they can tell me that ratio.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮面的是创始人而不是招聘人，把它换成「哪一类客户需求最常逼你们改架构」，能拿到更深的答案。
optionMeanings: 问工作构成与工程师的客户参与度。
问行业属性与加班强度。
问他们的 AI 落地计划。
问团队人数与招聘节奏。
optionMeanings_en: Ask about the work mix and engineers' customer exposure.
Ask about industry traits and overtime.
Ask about their plans to adopt AI.
Ask about headcount and hiring pace.
optionDirectness: 比例决定我每天写新代码还是改老流程。
把话题带向工作强度，容易被读成先谈条件。
替对方规划路线图，显得没研究过合规行业的落地约束。
官网已经给了答案，重复问会暴露功课没做。
optionDirectness_en: The ratio decides whether I write new code or patch old flows every day.
It steers toward workload and reads as negotiating conditions first.
Planning their roadmap for them signals no research into compliance constraints.
The website already answered it, so repeating it exposes missing prep.
optionScenarioImpacts: 拿到最能决定去留的一个数字，还顺带问出客户接触面。
对方会给一个安全的官方回答，信息量接近零。
他要么礼貌敷衍，要么解释监管为什么不让这么干。
浪费一个名额去确认一条公开信息。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You get the single number that most decides your answer, plus customer exposure.
You get a safe official answer with almost no information in it.
He either deflects politely or explains why regulation blocks it.
You spend a slot confirming something already public.

q: 任何公司、任何一轮都能用的两个兜底反问是什么？
q_en: What are the two fallback questions that work at any company, in any round?
text: 兜底一：加入之后有什么让你意外、在外面{{看不到}}的？兜底二：决定做什么是产品{{自上而下}}定，还是工程师有很强的话语权？
text_en: Fallback one: what surprised you after joining that you {{couldn't see}} from the outside? Fallback two: does product decide {{top-down}}, or do engineers have a strong voice in what gets built?
why: 这两个问题不依赖对这家公司的研究，任何一轮都能用；第一个逼出真实体验，第二个直接决定我进去后能不能参与决策。
why_en: Neither needs company research and both work in any round — the first pulls out lived experience, the second tells me whether engineers actually get a say.

scenario: 同一个 loop 里你会分别见到招聘人、招聘经理（HM）、以及未来的同级工程师。你手上只有一组准备好的问题。
scenario_en: In one loop you'll meet the recruiter, the hiring manager, and a future peer engineer. You have one prepared set of questions.
q: 这三类面试官分别最该问什么？
q_en: What should you ask each of these three interviewers?
options: 三轮都问同一组问题，保证口径一致，看谁答得最实在、互相有没有出入。
招聘人问岗位来历与流程，HM 问未来半年的优先级，同级工程师问日常真实怎么运作。
只在 HM 那轮准备问题，其他两轮说「前面已经解答了」来省时间。
把最尖锐的问题（比如上一个做这个岗位的人为什么走）留到最后一轮问最资深的那个人。
options_en: Ask all three the same set for consistency, and see who answers most honestly or contradicts the others.
Ask the recruiter about role history and process, the hiring manager about the next six months, and the peer about day-to-day reality.
Only prepare questions for the hiring manager round and say "that's already been covered" in the other two.
Save the sharpest question — like why the last person in this role left — for the most senior interviewer at the end.
tradeoff: 按角色分工提问 vs 三轮同一组：同一组省准备时间，代价是每轮都问到对方答不了的层级，拿回来的都是转述。
why: 问题要按对方能答的层级分：岗位来历只有招聘人清楚，未来半年优先级只有 HM 说了算，日常怎么运作只有同级工程师说得准。
why_en: Match each question to who can actually answer it — the recruiter owns role history, the hiring manager owns the next six months, and peers own the day-to-day.
whenOtherWins: 如果一整个 loop 只有一位面试官，那就必须把三层问题压进那一轮，并按「日常 → 半年 → 岗位来历」的顺序问。
optionMeanings: 三轮复用同一组问题做交叉验证。
按角色把问题分到能回答的人。
只为 HM 准备，其余两轮跳过。
把敏感问题留给最资深的人。
optionMeanings_en: Reuse one set across all three to cross-check answers.
Split questions by who can answer them.
Prepare only for the hiring manager and skip the rest.
Save sensitive questions for the most senior person.
optionDirectness: 交叉验证有价值，但代价是两轮拿到的都是二手转述。
每个人只被问他有第一手答案的事。
跳过的那两轮同样在写评价，「没问题」会被记下来。
岗位为什么空出来，招聘人第一轮就能直接回答。
optionDirectness_en: Cross-checking has value, but two of the rounds hand back second-hand accounts.
Each person is only asked what they have first-hand knowledge of.
The skipped rounds also write feedback, and "no questions" gets recorded there too.
Why the seat opened up is something the recruiter can answer in round one.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同一问题被转述三遍，我依然不知道日常什么样。
三轮各拿一层信息，拼起来是完整判断。
两轮留下不好奇的记录，还白丢两次拿信息的机会。
尖锐问题拖到最后，前面所有回答都少了这层背景。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The same question gets paraphrased three times and you still don't know the day-to-day.
Each round gives one layer and together they form a complete picture.
Two rounds log you as incurious and waste two chances to learn.
Holding the sharp question to the end leaves every earlier answer missing that context.

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘经理，你进去后的直属上级，决定团队未来半年做什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HM stands for hiring manager, the person you'd report to and who sets the team's priorities for the next six months.

scenario: Alex AI 面试官刚回答完你的团队结构问题：30 人、7 名工程师、扁平层级、每个工程师都直接和客户交流。
scenario_en: The Alex AI interviewer just answered your team-structure question: 30 people, 7 engineers, flat hierarchy, every engineer talks to customers directly.
q: 哪个追问是从他这句话里长出来的？
q_en: Which follow-up actually grows out of what he just said?
options: 你们工程师大概多久发一次版？CI/CD 是怎么搭起来的？
7 个工程师是不是有点少？你们计划招到多少人、什么时候补齐这几个坑？
你说工程师直接和客户交流——通常是陪着参加销售电话，还是异步看产品反馈？
扁平层级听起来挺好——那晋升和职级怎么评、多久评一次？
options_en: How often do your engineers ship? How is CI/CD set up?
Isn't 7 engineers a bit thin? How many are you hiring and when will those gaps be filled?
You said engineers talk to customers directly — is that sitting in on sales calls, or async through product feedback?
Flat hierarchy sounds good — how do promotions and levels get decided, and how often?
tradeoff: 顺着他的原话追问 vs 换一个新问题：新问题安全，代价是他刚交出的那条真实信息没被用上，听着像在念清单。
why: 好的追问要复述他刚说的那个具体事实，再给两条可选路径让他好答——这证明我在消化回答，而不是照着纸念下一条。
why_en: A good follow-up quotes the exact fact he just gave and offers two concrete paths, which proves I'm processing his answer instead of reading the next line off my paper.
whenOtherWins: 如果他的回答很短、没有可抓的具体事实，那就直接问一个新的实质问题，别把追问架在空气上。
optionMeanings: 转向发布节奏与工程流水线。
质疑人手是否够，转向招聘计划。
抓住「直接和客户交流」往下挖一层。
抓住「扁平」转向晋升与职级。
optionMeanings_en: Pivot to release cadence and the build pipeline.
Question whether headcount is enough and pivot to hiring plans.
Take "talks to customers directly" and dig one layer down.
Take "flat" and pivot to promotions and levels.
optionDirectness: 是个好问题，但和他刚给的信息没有关系，属于换话题。
把他给的事实当成问题来质疑，容易让对方转成防守。
复述原话再给两条路径，对方能一句话答清。
扁平确实是他说的，但落点变成我的待遇而不是团队运作。
optionDirectness_en: A fine question, but unrelated to what he just said — it's a topic change.
It treats his fact as a problem and pushes him into defending the team.
Quoting him and offering two paths lets him answer in one sentence.
"Flat" is his word, but the landing point becomes my career, not how the team works.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对话重启一次，他刚交出的信息被浪费。
气氛微妙，他开始解释而不是分享。
他会讲出具体场景，我立刻知道工程师离客户多近。
话题从团队滑到我的晋升，早了一步。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The conversation restarts and the information he just gave goes unused.
The mood tightens and he starts justifying rather than sharing.
He describes a concrete scene and you learn how close engineers really are to customers.
The topic slides from the team to my promotion, one step too early.

q: 实质追问的固定句式模板是什么？
q_en: What's the fixed template for a substantive follow-up question?
text: 追问模板：「你刚说{{他的原话}}——这通常怎么发生的？是 {{A}} 还是 {{B}}？」先复述，再给两条具体路径。
text_en: Follow-up template: "You said {{their exact words}} — how does that usually happen, {{A}} or {{B}}?" Quote it back first, then offer two concrete paths.
why: 复述原话证明我在听，两条候选路径把开放题变成好答的选择题——对方答得越具体，我拿到的判断信息越多。
why_en: Quoting their words proves I listened, and two candidate paths turn an open question into an easy choice that gets me a far more concrete answer.

scenario: 面试超时，面试官说「我们还有 3 分钟，你有什么想问的」。你纸上有两个问题：90 天成功标准、团队最大的未定技术决策。
scenario_en: The interview ran over and the interviewer says "we have three minutes, any questions?" Your paper has two: the 90-day success bar, and the biggest open technical decision.
q: 只够问一个，问哪个？
q_en: There's only room for one — which do you ask?
options: 两个都问，语速加快，争取 3 分钟塞完再补一句谢谢。
都不问了，说「时间不够，我邮件发给你」，把两个问题都推到会后。
换成问流程：后面还有几轮、下一轮谁面、大概什么时候能出结果，反正 3 分钟问不深。
问 90 天成功标准——答案短、可落地，还顺带让他说出对这个岗位的期待。
options_en: Ask both, talk faster, and try to cram them into three minutes plus a thank-you.
Ask neither — say "we're short on time, I'll email these" and push both to after the call.
Switch to process: rounds left, who's next, when you'll hear back, since three minutes can't go deep anyway.
Ask the 90-day success bar — short answer, concrete, and it makes him state his expectations for the role.
tradeoff: 只问一个高密度问题 vs 两个都塞：塞两个显得准备充分，代价是两个都被匆匆答完，我一个都没听清。
why: 时间被压缩时选那个「答案短但信息密度高」的问题：90 天成功标准一句话能答完，还逼他说出对这个岗位的真实期待。
why_en: When time is squeezed, pick the question with a short answer and high information density — the 90-day bar takes one sentence and forces him to state real expectations.
whenOtherWins: 如果他前面已经详细讲过职责和期待，那这 3 分钟该留给「团队最大的未定技术决策」，因为只有它是新信息。
optionMeanings: 两问都塞进 3 分钟。
全部推到会后邮件。
改问流程与时间线。
只问 90 天成功标准。
optionMeanings_en: Cram both into three minutes.
Push everything to a follow-up email.
Switch to process and timeline.
Ask only the 90-day success bar.
optionDirectness: 赶时间提问会让两个答案都变成敷衍的一句话。
邮件里对方回得更短更官方，现场那次是最好的机会。
流程本来就该问招聘人，用掉最后 3 分钟太可惜。
答案一句话说得完，还能顺出他对这个岗位的期待。
optionDirectness_en: Rushing both turns each answer into a throwaway line.
Email replies come back shorter and more official; the live moment is the best shot.
Process belongs to the recruiter anyway, so spending the last three minutes on it is a waste.
It's answerable in one sentence and surfaces his expectations for the role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 两个问题都被压成一句，等于都没问。
会后回复更官方，现场的坦率消失了。
结束时我对这份工作依然一无所知。
三分钟内拿到一条能直接判断匹配度的信息。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both questions get compressed into one line, so neither was really asked.
The written reply is more guarded and the live candor is gone.
You end the call still knowing nothing about the job.
In three minutes you get one fact you can judge fit against.

scenario: 你为 Daisy 这一轮准备了两个问题，都是技术栈：用哪个模型、选了哪家向量库。面试官是产品向的工程负责人。
scenario_en: You prepared two questions for the Daisy round, both about the stack: which model, which vector database. The interviewer is a product-facing engineering lead.
q: 该把其中一个换成什么问题？
q_en: Which one should you swap out, and for what?
options: 换成薪资和职级区间，早点确认双方在不在一个范围内。
换成产品层面的：这个 AI 功能上线后，改变了团队对「可靠性」的思考方式吗？
换成公司层面的：你们最近这轮融资准备怎么花、下一轮大概什么时候启动？
不换——技术栈问题最能显示我懂技术，两个都问完，再看有没有时间加问别的。
options_en: Swap in compensation and level range, to check early whether you're in the same ballpark.
Swap in a product-level question: after this AI feature shipped, did it change how the team thinks about reliability?
Swap in a company-level one: how will this round of funding be spent, and when does the next raise start?
Don't swap — stack questions best show that I know the tech; ask both and add more if there's time.
tradeoff: 留一个产品问题 vs 两个都问技术栈：技术栈显得懂行，代价是全场没有一句话显示我在想这东西对用户意味着什么。
why: 每场至少留一个产品层面的问题：技术栈的答案 JD 上就有，产品问题才显示我在想这个东西对用户和团队意味着什么。
why_en: Every interview keeps at least one product-level question, because the stack is already in the posting while a product question shows I'm thinking about what it means for users.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮明确是底层技术深挖、面试官是基础设施负责人，技术栈问题反而正确——但仍要留一个产品问题收尾。
optionMeanings: 改问薪资与职级区间。
改问该功能如何改变团队的判断。
改问融资用途与下一轮时间。
维持两个技术栈问题不变。
optionMeanings_en: Switch to compensation and level range.
Switch to how the feature changed the team's judgment.
Switch to how funding is spent and the next raise.
Keep both stack questions as they are.
optionDirectness: 适合和招聘人谈，向工程负责人开口会打断技术对话。
只有真在用这个产品的人答得出来，答案无法从公开材料抄。
适合早期尽调，而这里我更需要判断进去做什么。
两个同类问题会把整场收窄成一次工具核对。
optionDirectness_en: Belongs with the recruiter; raising it with an engineering lead derails the technical thread.
Only someone actually shipping the product can answer, and it can't be copied from public material.
Fits early-stage diligence, but here I need to judge what I'd be building.
Two questions of the same kind shrink the whole round into a tooling checklist.
optionScenarioImpacts: 技术负责人无法回答，气氛也变尴尬。
他会讲一次真实的教训，我看到团队怎么做判断。
得到一段融资叙事，和我的日常工作无关。
全场没有一句话显示我关心用户。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The engineering lead can't answer and the moment turns awkward.
He recounts a real lesson and you see how the team makes judgment calls.
You get a funding narrative unrelated to your daily work.
Nothing in the whole call shows you care about the user.

q: 产品层面反问的模板长什么样？
q_en: What does a product-level question template look like?
text: 产品层面模板：「你们的{{核心功能}}上线后，改变了团队对{{可靠性 / 信任}}的思考方式吗？」——问它让你们{{改变了什么判断}}，不是问它用了什么技术。
text_en: Product-level template: "After your {{core feature}} shipped, did it change how the team thinks about {{reliability or trust}}?" Ask what judgment it changed, not what technology it uses.
why: 技术栈问的是「你们用什么」，产品问题问的是「它让你们改变了什么判断」——后者只有真在做这个产品的人答得出来。
why_en: A stack question asks what they use; a product question asks what changed in how they decide, and only someone actually building it can answer that.

scenario: Assembled 的工程经理 Jake 刚说，他们的文化价值观是 "Assembled is my team"：每个人对整体结果负责，不只做分工内那块。下一题问你看重什么样的公司。
scenario_en: Assembled's engineering manager Jake just said their cultural value is "Assembled is my team" — everyone owns the whole outcome, not just their slice. The next question asks what you look for in a company.
q: 你的下一个回答该怎么开头？
q_en: How should your next answer open?
options: 照着原稿说：我看重责任心和清晰的沟通，然后展开讲两个例子。
先夸一句「你们这个文化听起来真好」，然后照原稿讲自己看重什么，不做连接。
直接接住：你刚说的那条正是我在找的——我见过工程师越出分工时事情推得更快。
反过来问他：这条价值观在日常里具体怎么落地？先把话题从我自己身上移开。
options_en: Read the script: I value accountability and clear communication, then give two examples.
Compliment it first — "that culture sounds great" — then run the same script with no connection made.
Catch it directly: what you just said is exactly what I'm looking for — I've seen work move faster when engineers step past their slice.
Turn it around: how does that value actually show up day to day? Move the focus off yourself first.
tradeoff: 引用他的价值观 vs 照原稿答：原稿安全，代价是刚出现的连接点被浪费，回答听起来对谁都能说。
why: 面试官主动说出价值观，等于递给我一个可以引用的钩子；下一个回答不接，就等于告诉他我在念稿、没在听。
why_en: When an interviewer names their cultural value they hand me a hook to quote, and not using it in the very next answer tells them I'm reciting rather than listening.
whenOtherWins: 如果他说的价值观你并不认同，就别硬引用——诚实说自己更看重什么，比假装对齐更安全，也更经得起追问。
optionMeanings: 按原稿讲自己看重什么。
先夸一句，再回到原稿。
引用他刚说的价值观并接上自己的经验。
把问题反抛回去请他展开。
optionMeanings_en: Run the prepared answer about what you value.
Compliment it, then return to the script.
Quote his value and attach your own experience.
Bounce the question back and ask him to elaborate.
optionDirectness: 内容不算错，但和三十秒前那句话没有任何交叉。
夸奖不是引用，他听到的仍然是一段通用回答。
把他的原话变成我答案的起点，连接当场成立。
反问很好，但用在这里等于回避了他刚问我的问题。
optionDirectness_en: Not wrong, but it never intersects with what he said thirty seconds ago.
A compliment isn't a quote — he still hears a generic answer.
His own words become the opening of my answer and the link lands immediately.
Asking back is fine elsewhere, but here it dodges the question he just asked.
optionScenarioImpacts: 他会觉得我准备过，但没在听他说话。
礼貌收下，记不住任何东西。
他听到自己的价值观被我的经历验证了一遍。
他要重新把问题问一遍，节奏被打断。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: He concludes you prepared but weren't listening to him.
Politely received and instantly forgotten.
He hears his own value confirmed by your experience.
He has to re-ask the question and the rhythm breaks.

q: 面试官刚说出公司价值观，引用它的句式是什么？
q_en: The interviewer just named a company value — what's the sentence that quotes it back?
text: 引用句式：「你刚说的{{那条价值观}}正好对上我在找的——我在 Meta 和 TikTok 都见过，工程师{{越出分工}}去负责结果时，事情推得快很多。」
text_en: Quote-back line: "{{That value you just named}} is exactly what I'm looking for — at Meta and TikTok I saw things move much faster when engineers {{stepped past their slice}} to own the outcome."
why: 引用要落到一个我真见过的场景，而不是复述他的话；重复他的原话是恭维，加上我的证据才是连接。
why_en: The quote has to land on a scene I actually lived through — repeating his words is flattery, adding my evidence is what makes it a connection.

scenario: Pinpoint 面试里你提到在中国做过一个培训系统，面试官立刻接话："like a training system, so we do"。你只回了 "yeah, yeah"。
scenario_en: In the Pinpoint interview you mentioned building a training system in China, and the interviewer immediately said "like a training system, so we do." You just answered "yeah, yeah."
q: 那一秒正确的回应是什么？
q_en: What was the right response in that second?
options: 一句话说清共同点：两边都是给非技术用户搭结构化流程，我在那边学到了 X。
"yeah, yeah" 之后继续把原来的故事讲完，等他真的追问了再展开这个共同点。
顺势问他：那你们的培训系统现在做到哪一步了？把话题交回给他。
说「对，很像」，然后把话题跳到你更想讲的 TikTok 项目上去。
options_en: Name the overlap in one line: both are structured workflows for non-technical users, and here's what I learned there.
Say "yeah, yeah," finish the original story, and expand on the overlap only if he asks again.
Turn it around: how far along is your training system? Hand the topic back to him.
Say "yes, very similar" and jump to the TikTok project you'd rather talk about.
tradeoff: 当场点破共同点 vs 等他再问：等待不会失分，代价是这个免费的连接窗口两秒后就关上，之后再提就变刻意。
why: 面试官说出「我们也做这个」的那一秒是免费的连接窗口；"yeah, yeah" 把它关掉了。用一句话点出共同的抽象模式，再落回我学到什么。
why_en: The second an interviewer says "we do that too" is a free connection window, and "yeah, yeah" closes it — name the shared pattern in one line, then land on what I learned.
whenOtherWins: 如果他只是顺口一提、马上继续讲自己的内容，就别打断；把这个共同点留到反问环节，用一个问题把它接回来。
optionMeanings: 当场说出共同的抽象模式并落回自己。
先讲完原故事，等他再问。
把问题反抛给他讲他们的系统。
承认相似后转去别的项目。
optionMeanings_en: Name the shared pattern now and land it on yourself.
Finish the original story and wait for him to ask again.
Bounce it back and let him describe their system.
Acknowledge the similarity and pivot to another project.
optionDirectness: 抽象出共同模式，这个连接就从巧合变成论据。
等待的成本是那扇窗两秒后就关了，再提显得刻意。
适合他明显想炫耀自家产品时；这里他是在向我确认。
承认相似却不说明为什么相似，等于放弃这条线索。
optionDirectness_en: Naming the shared pattern turns the coincidence into an argument for you.
Waiting costs you the window, which shuts within seconds and feels forced afterwards.
Fits when he clearly wants to show off their product; here he's checking with you.
Agreeing it's similar without saying why abandons the thread entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts: 他记住我是「做过同类东西的人」，不只是候选人。
故事讲完时那个时机已经过去了。
他讲了三分钟他们的系统，我的经历没被记住。
跳走后他不会再回到这个共同点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: He remembers you as someone who has built the same thing, not just a candidate.
By the time the story ends, the moment has passed.
He talks about their system for three minutes and your experience goes unremembered.
Once you jump away he never returns to the overlap.

scenario: 面试官刚说「我们也做这个」，你要在一句话里把连接说明白，而不是回一句「对，很像」。
scenario_en: The interviewer just said "we do that too," and you want to make the connection explicit in one breath instead of answering "yes, very similar."
q: 把「抓住连接时机」的四拍排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four beats of seizing an alignment moment in the right order.
steps: 落回自己：那段经历里我学到的是什么
先确认他说的那个词：对，我做的就是这类东西
抽象出共同点：两边都是给非技术用户搭结构化流程
接回他们正在做的事：你刚描述的这块也是同一个模式
why: 连接不是「对，很像」四个字，而是四拍：确认 → 说出共同的抽象模式 → 我在那学到什么 → 接回你们正在做的事。
why_en: A connection isn't "yes, similar" — it's four beats: confirm, name the shared pattern, say what I learned, then tie it back to what they're building.

scenario: Eclipse 的联创 Johnny 在 0:33 说 "we're getting an office in Brooklyn"。你听成了 Berkeley，接着问「你们打算之后搬去 Berkeley 吗」。
scenario_en: At 0:33 Eclipse co-founder Johnny said "we're getting an office in Brooklyn." You heard Berkeley and asked "so you're planning to move to Berkeley later?"
q: 没听清专有名词时，正确做法是什么？
q_en: What's the right move when you didn't catch a proper noun?
options: 先按自己听到的那个词往下说，等对方纠正了再改口，尽量不打断他的节奏。
跳过这个地名，只回应句子里其他听懂的部分，装作没注意到这个词。
先记下来，等这一轮结束前再问「刚才那个城市是哪儿来着」，避免当场打断。
当场确认："sorry, did you say Brooklyn?"
options_en: Keep going with the word you thought you heard and correct course only if they fix it, so you don't break their flow.
Skip the place name and respond only to the parts of the sentence you did catch, acting like you didn't notice.
Note it down and ask near the end of the round which city he meant, to avoid interrupting in the moment.
Confirm on the spot: "sorry, did you say Brooklyn?"
tradeoff: 当场确认 vs 硬着头皮往下讲：不打断保住了流畅，代价是接下来每一句都建在一个错词上，越走越远。
why: 专有名词听错还继续往下讲，等于告诉对方我不在这场对话里；当场一句确认只花两秒，没有人会因此扣分。
why_en: Running with a misheard proper noun tells them I'm not really in the conversation, while a two-second check costs nothing and no interviewer marks you down for it.
whenOtherWins: 如果没听清的是不影响判断的闲聊细节（比如某个第三方的人名），可以顺过去；地名、公司名、产品名必须当场确认。
optionMeanings: 带着错词继续讲，等对方纠正。
绕开这个词只答别的部分。
记下来，等本轮快结束再确认。
立刻用一句话确认这个词。
optionMeanings_en: Carry on with the wrong word and wait to be corrected.
Route around the word and answer only the rest.
Write it down and confirm near the end of the round.
Confirm the word immediately in one line.
optionDirectness: 后面每句话都建在错词上，纠正的代价随时间变大。
绕开听起来像敷衍，对方也无法判断我有没有听懂。
延后确认时，基于这个词的对话已经进行了十分钟。
两秒成本换掉整段对话建在错词上的风险。
optionDirectness_en: Every later sentence rests on the wrong word, and the cost of fixing it grows with time.
Routing around sounds evasive and leaves them unsure whether you understood.
By the time you confirm, ten minutes of conversation already rest on that word.
Two seconds of cost removes the risk of building the whole exchange on a wrong word.
optionScenarioImpacts: 他听到 Berkeley，知道我根本没在听。
他不确定我懂没懂，只好自己再解释一遍。
错误已经影响了中间十分钟的对话内容。
他确认一遍，对话继续，还显得我在认真听。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: He hears "Berkeley" and knows you weren't listening.
He can't tell whether you understood and ends up explaining again.
The error has already shaped ten minutes of conversation.
He repeats it, the call continues, and you come across as attentive.

q: 听不清专有名词时的固定修复句是什么？哪些词必须当场问？
q_en: What's the fixed repair line for a missed proper noun, and which words must be confirmed live?
text: 固定修复句：「{{sorry, did you say Brooklyn?}}」——只在{{地名 / 公司名 / 产品名}}这类会影响后续回答的词上打断，两秒问清。
text_en: Repair line: "{{sorry, did you say Brooklyn?}}" Only interrupt for {{place, company, or product names}} — the words that shape everything you say next.
why: 把打断限制在会影响后续回答的专有名词上，既不会显得频繁打断，也不会让整段对话建在一个听错的词上。
why_en: Limiting interruptions to proper nouns that shape my next answers keeps me from interrupting constantly while never letting a whole exchange rest on a misheard word.

scenario: GenLogs 招聘人问「你了解我们做什么吗」。你已经花 15 分钟看过官网和一篇新闻，要给一个有观点的回答。
scenario_en: The GenLogs recruiter asks "what do you know about us?" You've spent 15 minutes on their site and one news piece, and want an answer with a point of view.
q: 把「你了解我们吗」的四拍排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four beats of answering "what do you know about us" in the right order.
steps: 连接自己的经验：我做过和这一点最接近的是什么
一句话说清他们做什么：你们是给某类客户解决某个问题
用一个问题收尾，把话头交回给对方
挑一点他们的做法说出看法：我最感兴趣的是你们选了 C 而不是 D
why: 纯产品描述只证明我打开过官网首页；要有一句「我最感兴趣的是…」的判断，再连回我的经验，最后用一个问题把话头交回去。
why_en: A plain product description only proves I opened the homepage — I need one line of judgment, then a link to my own experience, then a question that hands the floor back.

scenario: GenLogs 招聘人问「你了解我们做什么吗」。你把官网首页那段产品描述准确背了出来，之后没有任何自己的判断。
scenario_en: The GenLogs recruiter asked "what do you know about us?" You accurately recited the homepage product blurb and added no judgment of your own.
q: 这段回答该补上什么？
q_en: What is this answer missing?
options: 补上公司融资额、员工人数、创始人背景，显得功课做得更细。
补一句自己的看法和一次经验连接，再用一个问题收尾。
补一句「所以我觉得这个方向前景很好、很有潜力」，把热情表达出来。
什么都不用补，产品描述准确就够了，观点留到技术轮再说。
options_en: Add funding raised, headcount, and founder backgrounds to show deeper homework.
Add one line of your own view plus one link to your experience, then close with a question.
Add "so I think this space has a lot of potential" to convey enthusiasm.
Add nothing — an accurate product description is enough, save opinions for the technical round.
tradeoff: 加判断与连接 vs 只描述产品：只描述不会说错，代价是任何人读一遍首页都能给出同样的回答。
why: 只描述产品等于只读了官网首页；要加一句「我最感兴趣的是你们选了 X 而不是 Y」的判断、一次经验连接，再用问题收尾。
why_en: Describing the product only proves I read the homepage — add one line of judgment about a choice they made, one link to my experience, and close with a question.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方只是快速核对你有没有做功课（比如 5 分钟的 cold outreach），一句准确描述加一个问题就够了。
optionMeanings: 补更多可查的事实数据。
补一句判断加一次经验连接。
补一句对赛道前景的表态。
维持纯产品描述不变。
optionMeanings_en: Add more lookup-able facts and figures.
Add a judgment plus one experience link.
Add an enthusiastic take on the market.
Keep the plain product description.
optionDirectness: 事实越多越像背书，仍然没有一句属于我的判断。
判断显示我读懂了，连接显示我能上手。
「前景很好」对任何公司都成立，不构成观点。
准确不等于有见解，对方无法区分我和其他候选人。
optionDirectness_en: More facts read as more memorization and still contain no view of my own.
The judgment shows I understood it and the link shows I could contribute.
"Great potential" is true of any company, so it isn't a point of view.
Accuracy isn't insight, and they can't tell you apart from other candidates.
optionScenarioImpacts: 听起来像在念一份公司简报。
他会顺着我的判断继续聊，对话真正开始。
礼貌的空话，不会被写进任何记录。
回答无懈可击，也毫无记忆点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It sounds like reading a company briefing aloud.
He picks up your judgment and the conversation actually starts.
A polite empty line that makes it into no write-up.
The answer is flawless and completely unmemorable.

q: 每次面试前 15 分钟的公司功课清单是什么？
q_en: What's the 15-minute company-research checklist before every interview?
text: 会前 15 分钟：官网 + LinkedIn About + 一篇{{近期新闻}}；确认公司名{{怎么念}}；说得出核心产品和{{一个竞争对手}}。
text_en: Fifteen minutes before the call: the website, the LinkedIn About, and one {{recent news item}}; check {{how the name is pronounced}}; be able to name the core product and {{one competitor}}.
why: 反问和「你了解我们吗」都建在这 15 分钟上：没有具体事实，问题只能问得很泛，回答也只能复述首页。
why_en: Both my questions and my "what do you know about us" answer rest on those fifteen minutes — without a concrete fact I can only ask vaguely and recite the homepage.

scenario: Eclipse Performance 是 pre-seed 的运动可穿戴公司：已融 150 万美元，2 名全职创始人加 2 名顾问。通话末尾轮到你提问。
scenario_en: Eclipse Performance is a pre-seed sports-wearable company: 1.5M raised, two full-time founders plus two advisors. At the end of the call it's your turn to ask.
q: 加入 2 人团队前，反问该覆盖什么？
q_en: Before joining a two-person team, what should your questions cover?
options: 只问技术问题——融资和人数听起来太像在质疑他们，早期阶段容易冒犯人。
只问产品愿景和三年规划，早期公司一上来谈钱显得不够有信念。
团队现在多少人、融到哪一轮、接下来怎么分工——先把风险摸清。
问期权池占比、行权价、稀释条款这些细节，先把回报算清楚再说。
options_en: Ask only technical questions — funding and headcount sound like doubting them, which is easy to take badly this early.
Ask only about product vision and the three-year plan, since talking money this early looks like weak conviction.
Team size, funding round, and how work will be divided — get the risk mapped first.
Ask about option pool percentage, strike price, and dilution terms, so the payoff is clear up front.
tradeoff: 问团队与融资 vs 只问产品愿景：只谈愿景气氛更好，代价是我在没有任何风险数据的情况下考虑加入一家 2 人公司。
why: 加入 2 人公司是在承担公司级风险，问团队规模、融资阶段、分工不是冒犯，恰恰说明我认真在评估——这一轮我做对了，要保持。
why_en: Joining a two-person company means taking company-level risk, so asking about size, stage, and how work splits isn't rude — it shows I'm seriously evaluating, and I got this one right.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 500 人以上的成熟公司，融资阶段基本是公开信息，这几个名额该换成团队优先级和决策方式。
optionMeanings: 回避融资与人数，只谈技术。
只谈愿景与三年规划。
问人数、融资阶段与分工。
问期权池、行权价与稀释。
optionMeanings_en: Avoid funding and headcount, stay technical.
Talk only about vision and the three-year plan.
Ask about size, stage, and how work divides.
Ask about option pool, strike price, and dilution.
optionDirectness: 创始人预期候选人会问这些，回避反而像没认真考虑加入。
愿景在 pre-seed 阶段一定动听，无法用来判断风险。
这三项决定我进去后大概能干多久、干什么。
股权细节属于 offer 阶段，第一次通话问会显得只算回报。
optionDirectness_en: Founders expect these questions, so dodging them reads as not seriously considering the jump.
Vision always sounds good at pre-seed, so it can't tell you anything about risk.
These three decide how long you'd last there and what you'd actually do.
Equity detail belongs at offer stage; on a first call it reads as pure payoff math.
optionScenarioImpacts: 他无法判断我是否真的在考虑这个机会。
聊得愉快，但我依然不知道公司能撑多久。
拿到判断这家能不能去的三项基本事实。
话题转向谈判，第一通电话就变紧张。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: He can't tell whether you're genuinely considering the opportunity.
A pleasant chat that still leaves you blind to how long the company lasts.
You leave with the three basic facts that decide whether to proceed.
The call turns into a negotiation and tightens on the first contact.

scenario: 一家 pre-seed 公司邀你去做第 3 号工程师。你要判断这份工作大概能存活多久。
scenario_en: A pre-seed company wants you as engineer number three. You need to judge how long this job is likely to last.
q: 问 runway 时，什么数字算安全、什么数字必须追问？
q_en: When you ask about runway, which number is comfortable and which one forces a follow-up?
text: runway（现有现金还能撑几个月）：{{18-24 个月}}是常见的安全线；不足 {{12 个月}}就必须追问下一轮的融资计划和目标投资人。
text_en: Runway (how many months the current cash lasts): {{18-24 months}} is the usual comfort line; under {{12 months}} you must follow up on the next raise and which investors they're targeting.
why: runway 直接决定我进去后大概多久要再找工作；不足 12 个月还问不出下一轮计划，就是在赌一个我完全没有数据的东西。
why_en: Runway decides how soon I'd be job-hunting again, and under twelve months with no answer on the next raise means betting on something I have no data about.

termDefinitions.meaning: 公司账上现金按当前烧钱速度还能维持的月数，早期公司最核心的存活指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Runway is how many months a company's cash lasts at its current burn rate, the core survival number for an early-stage startup.

scenario: Pinpoint 是 15 人的金融合规创业公司，你的目标区间是 16-20 万美元。你已经进到 recruiter screen 了。
scenario_en: Pinpoint is a 15-person financial-compliance startup and your target range is $160-200K. You're already in the recruiter screen.
q: 薪资现实检验该放在流程的哪一步？
q_en: At which point in the process does the compensation reality check belong?
options: 等拿到 offer 再谈，先把流程走完，反正谈崩了也没什么损失。
投递前就查同规模同行业的区间；对不上就不投，别浪费双方时间。
终面时再问，问太早显得只关心钱，可能影响面试官的印象。
不查区间，先拿到 offer 当筹码，再回去和别家公司抬价。
options_en: Wait for the offer and negotiate then — finish the process, since a failed negotiation costs nothing.
Check the range for this size and industry before applying; if it doesn't match, don't apply.
Ask at the final round — asking early looks money-focused and may hurt the interviewer's impression.
Don't check at all; get the offer as leverage and use it to push another company's number up.
tradeoff: 投递前检验 vs 走完流程再谈：走完流程保留了拿 offer 的可能，代价是四五轮面试后才发现区间根本对不上。
why: 15 人的金融合规创业公司大概率给不到 16-20 万；结构性不匹配还走完全程，浪费双方时间，也损耗我在这个招聘人那里的信誉。
why_en: A 15-person compliance startup almost certainly can't reach 160-200K, and running the full loop on a structural mismatch burns both sides' time and my credibility with that recruiter.
whenOtherWins: 如果这家的产品或阶段是你特别想要的，可以主动降低区间去投——但要在第一通电话就说清楚，而不是拖到 offer 阶段。
optionMeanings: 推迟到 offer 阶段再谈。
投递前先做区间核对。
留到终面再开口。
不核对，把 offer 当谈判筹码。
optionMeanings_en: Defer the conversation to offer stage.
Check the range before applying.
Raise it only at the final round.
Skip the check and use the offer as leverage.
optionDirectness: 只有区间接近时才划算；差 40% 时前面几轮全是沉没成本。
公开的同规模区间足够判断，几分钟就能查完。
终面才发现不匹配，双方都已经投入四五轮。
拿别家 offer 抬价需要真心想去那家，否则风险很大。
optionDirectness_en: Only worth it when the ranges are close; a 40% gap makes every earlier round sunk cost.
Public ranges for this company size are enough and take a few minutes to check.
Discovering the mismatch at the final round means both sides already spent four or five rounds.
Using an offer as leverage only works if you'd genuinely take it, otherwise it backfires.
optionScenarioImpacts: 五轮之后才发现差 40%，双方都白忙。
对不上就不投，时间留给能成的公司。
招聘人会觉得我早该说，印象反而更差。
这个招聘人以后不会再给我推别的岗位。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You discover a 40% gap after five rounds and both sides wasted the effort.
A mismatch means you don't apply and the time goes to companies that can work.
The recruiter thinks you should have said so earlier, which hurts more than helps.
That recruiter stops sending you other roles in the future.

scenario: recruiter screen 里你还剩最后一个提问名额。这个岗位的 JD 写得很泛，你看不出它是新增的还是有人走了留下的。
scenario_en: One question slot left in the recruiter screen. The job description is vague and you can't tell whether the role is new or backfilling someone who left.
q: 问哪一句最能提前暴露风险？
q_en: Which single question surfaces risk earliest?
options: 团队现在的技术栈是什么？以后有没有换栈的计划？
你们的年假和远程政策是怎么样的？弹性大不大？
这个岗位的职级对应你们内部的哪一级？以后怎么晋升？
这个岗位是新增的还是有人离开留下的？上一个人做了多久？
options_en: What's the team's current stack, and are there plans to change it?
What's your vacation and remote policy, and how flexible is it?
Which internal level does this role map to, and how do promotions work?
Is this a new role or a backfill? How long did the last person stay?
why: 「新增还是替补 + 上一个人待了多久」一句话就问出团队是在扩张还是在流失；招聘人愿意如实回答，答案却最能预警。
why_en: Asking whether the role is new or a backfill and how long the last person stayed reveals in one line whether the team is growing or bleeding, and recruiters answer it honestly.
optionMeanings: 问技术栈现状与迁移计划。
问假期与远程弹性。
问职级映射与晋升路径。
问岗位来历与前任任期。
optionMeanings_en: Ask about the current stack and migration plans.
Ask about vacation and remote flexibility.
Ask about level mapping and the promotion path.
Ask about the role's origin and the predecessor's tenure.
optionDirectness: 技术栈会变，但换不换栈和团队健不健康无关。
福利在 offer package 里会写清楚，现在问不产生信息。
职级映射重要，但它反映的是我的位置，不是团队的稳定性。
前任任期短且没人接手，通常意味着期望或支持有问题。
optionDirectness_en: Stacks change, but whether they migrate says nothing about team health.
Benefits are spelled out in the offer package, so asking now adds nothing.
Level mapping matters, but it describes my position, not the team's stability.
A short predecessor tenure with no successor usually means broken expectations or support.
optionScenarioImpacts: 得到一份工具清单，风险信号一个都没看到。
话题偏向条件，风险仍然完全未知。
知道自己的职级，仍不知道团队在扩张还是流失。
一句话拿到扩张 / 流失的信号，还能顺势追问原因。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You get a tooling list and see no risk signal at all.
The topic drifts to conditions and the risk stays invisible.
You learn your level but still not whether the team is growing or bleeding.
One line gives you the growth-or-attrition signal and a natural follow-up on why.

q: Amazon loop 里 bar raiser 是谁？这对每一轮的反问意味着什么？
q_en: Who is the bar raiser in an Amazon loop, and what does that mean for your questions in every round?
text: Amazon 的 bar raiser 通常来自{{外组}}、和这个岗位没有利益关系，负责{{主持 debrief}}并拥有{{否决权}}；候选人当场分辨不出是谁。
text_en: Amazon's bar raiser usually comes from {{another org}} with no stake in the role, {{chairs the debrief}}, and holds a {{veto}}; candidates can't tell which interviewer it is.
why: 我在现场分不出谁是 bar raiser，而 debrief 会把各轮的书面记录拼成一个叙事——所以没有哪一轮可以「反正不重要」而不问问题。
why_en: I can't tell which interviewer is the bar raiser, and the debrief stitches every round's written record into one narrative, so no round gets a pass on asking real questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 从外组抽调的资深面试官，负责跨候选人横向定级把关，并主持面试后的 debrief。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a senior Amazon interviewer pulled from another org who guards the hiring bar across candidates and chairs the post-loop debrief.

termDefinitions.meaning: loop 结束后所有面试官开的评议会，把各轮书面反馈汇总成一个录用与否的结论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The debrief is the post-loop meeting where all interviewers merge their written feedback into a single hire-or-no-hire decision.

scenario: WOP 招聘人早前说过「我们还没到能从 Meta/TikTok 这种级别招人的阶段」，你当场已经正面接住了。现在到了反问环节。
scenario_en: Earlier the WOP recruiter said "we're not at the stage where we hire from Meta or TikTok yet," and you already addressed it head-on. Now it's the questions segment.
q: 这时的反问该用来做什么？
q_en: What should your questions do at this point?
options: 问「你们大概什么时候才会招到那个级别」，把级别这个话题继续往下追问。
避开级别不提，问一个安全的通用问题，别再刺激这个话题。
问「这个岗位前 90 天最想让人搞定哪一块」，用工作内容替换级别话题。
问「那我是不是不太合适」，直接请他给一个明确答复，省得双方来回猜。
options_en: Ask "when do you expect to hire at that level?" and keep pushing on the level thread.
Steer clear of level entirely and ask something safe and generic so you don't poke it again.
Ask "what do you most want this person to solve in the first 90 days?" and replace level with the work.
Ask "so am I not a fit?" and get a direct answer instead of both sides guessing.
tradeoff: 用工作内容替换级别 vs 继续争级别：继续争能问出他们的招聘规划，代价是整通电话都在谈头衔，而不是谈我能干的活。
why: 软拒绝接住之后还要用反问收口：问岗位前 90 天要解决什么，把对话从「他配不配这个级别」搬回「这摊活他能不能干」。
why_en: After catching a soft rejection I still need my questions to land it — asking what the first 90 days must solve moves the talk from my level back to the work itself.
whenOtherWins: 如果他已经说明这个岗位的预算和级别都定死、和你完全不重合，那就该问清楚有没有别的岗位，而不是继续争取这一个。
optionMeanings: 继续在级别话题上追问时间表。
回避级别，改问通用问题。
改问前 90 天要解决的问题。
直接请他给出是否合适的结论。
optionMeanings_en: Keep pushing on level and ask for their timeline.
Avoid level and ask something generic.
Ask what the first 90 days must solve.
Ask him to state outright whether you fit.
optionDirectness: 他的招聘规划和我能不能拿这个岗位没有关系。
回避让他保留原来的结论，我一句话都没改变它。
让他描述活，我就有机会接一句我做过最像的那件事。
在他还没决定时逼他表态，通常只会拿到一个「再看看」。
optionDirectness_en: Their hiring roadmap has nothing to do with whether I get this role.
Avoiding it leaves his conclusion intact and nothing I said moved it.
Making him describe the work gives me an opening to match my closest project.
Forcing a verdict before he's decided usually just gets a non-committal answer.
optionScenarioImpacts: 整通电话停留在头衔上，没人谈过这份工作。
他挂断时仍然认为我 over-positioned。
他讲完 90 天要解决什么，我立刻能接上匹配的经历。
把软拒绝推成硬拒绝，还失去了继续对话的余地。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The whole call stays on titles and nobody ever discusses the job.
He hangs up still thinking you're over-positioned.
He describes the first 90 days and you immediately match it to real work.
You turn a soft no into a hard no and lose the room to keep talking.

q: 接住软拒绝之后，用哪一句反问把话题拉回工作内容？
q_en: After catching a soft rejection, which question pulls the conversation back to the work?
text: 收口反问：「{{这个岗位前 90 天最想让人搞定的是哪一块？}}」——让他先描述活，我再接一句{{我做过最像的那件事}}。
text_en: Closing question: "{{What do you most want this person to solve in the first 90 days?}}" Let him describe the work first, then match it with {{the closest thing I've actually built}}.
why: 这句话把评价对象从「我的级别」换成「这摊活」；只要他开始描述工作内容，我就有一个具体的连接点可以接。
why_en: This swaps the thing being judged from my level to the job itself, and the moment he starts describing the work I have a concrete hook to connect to.

scenario: 结构化面试里每位面试官会在会后独立填一份评分表，其中一栏是对岗位的兴趣与投入度；Amazon 的 debrief 再把各轮记录汇总成一个叙事。
scenario_en: In a structured process every interviewer files a scorecard afterwards, and one line is interest in the role; Amazon's debrief then merges all rounds into one narrative.
q: 「候选人没有问题」会怎么被记下来？
q_en: How does "the candidate had no questions" get recorded?
options: 不会被记——反问不在任何一条评分维度里，它只是一个礼貌性的收尾环节而已。
会被记成时间管理问题，说明这一轮的节奏没控好。
进书面记录的「兴趣/投入」一栏，成为负面证据，并带进 debrief。
会被记成沟通能力不足，因为候选人没有主动发起话题。
options_en: It isn't recorded at all — questions are not a scored dimension anywhere, just a polite way to close the round.
It's logged as a time-management issue, meaning the round's pacing went off.
It lands in the written "interest / engagement" line as negative evidence and carries into the debrief.
It's logged as weak communication, since the candidate started no topics.
why: 评分表里有「对岗位的兴趣」一栏，「没有问题」就是这一栏的负面证据；debrief 把各轮书面记录拼成一个叙事，它跑不掉。
why_en: The scorecard has an interest-in-the-role line, "no questions" is the evidence that fills it negatively, and the debrief stitches every round's write-up into one narrative.
optionMeanings: 认为反问不进评分。
归到时间管理维度。
归到兴趣与投入维度并进 debrief。
归到沟通能力维度。
optionMeanings_en: Assume questions aren't scored.
File it under time management.
File it under interest and carry it to the debrief.
File it under communication skills.
optionDirectness: 结构化评分表普遍带兴趣栏，正是为了记这类观察。
节奏是面试官自己的责任，不会算到候选人头上。
面试官只有这一栏能承载「他对这份工作好不好奇」。
沟通看的是表达是否清楚，和有没有提问是两件事。
optionDirectness_en: Structured scorecards routinely carry an interest line precisely to hold this observation.
Pacing is the interviewer's own responsibility and isn't charged to the candidate.
This is the only line that can hold "was he curious about this job".
Communication measures clarity of expression, which is separate from asking questions.
optionScenarioImpacts: 以为不影响，于是连续六轮都不问。
归错维度，也就找不到真正要修的地方。
六轮的负面证据在 debrief 里叠成同一个结论。
误以为要练表达，实际要练的是准备问题。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Believing it doesn't matter is how six rounds in a row go unasked.
Filing it under the wrong dimension hides what actually needs fixing.
Six rounds of negative evidence stack into one conclusion at the debrief.
You practice delivery when what you needed was prepared questions.

scenario: 面试快结束，面试官问：「你对这个岗位有没有什么顾虑或者犹豫的地方？」你确实在意团队只有 7 个工程师、没有专职测试。
scenario_en: Near the end the interviewer asks, "any concerns or hesitations about this role?" You genuinely worry about 7 engineers and no dedicated QA.
q: 这个反过来的问题怎么答？
q_en: How do you answer this reversed question?
options: 说「暂时没有，都挺好的」，把疑虑留到 offer 阶段自己权衡。
把顾虑摊成一份完整的缺点清单：没有专职测试、人手不够、流程不成熟，请他逐条解释。
转成夸奖：我唯一的顾虑是怕自己成长太快，跟不上你们的节奏。
说出真实顾虑并附上你的假设：没有专职测试，我猜质量靠 code review 兜？
options_en: Say "none right now, it all sounds good" and weigh your doubts privately at offer stage.
Lay out a complete list of negatives — no dedicated QA, too few people, immature process — and ask him to address each one.
Turn it into a compliment: my only worry is growing so fast I can't keep up with you.
Name the real concern with your own hypothesis: with no dedicated QA, I'm guessing code review carries quality?
tradeoff: 说出真实顾虑 vs 说没有顾虑：说没有最安全，代价是放弃了让对方当场替我解决顾虑的唯一机会。
why: 「没有顾虑」放弃了让对方替我解决顾虑的机会；说出真实顾虑并附上自己的猜测，把它变成一个可讨论的技术问题，而不是抱怨。
why_en: Saying I have no concerns throws away the one chance to have them resolved — naming the real one with my own hypothesis turns it into a technical discussion rather than a complaint.
whenOtherWins: 如果顾虑是薪资或职级这类要和招聘人谈的事，就别在技术面提，留到招聘人那一轮说。
optionMeanings: 回答没有顾虑。
列一份缺点清单请他解释。
把顾虑包装成夸奖。
说出真实顾虑并给出自己的猜测。
optionMeanings_en: Answer that you have no concerns.
Present a list of negatives for him to address.
Dress the concern up as a compliment.
State the real concern plus your own hypothesis.
optionDirectness: 只有当你确实已经决定不去时才无所谓；否则等于放弃提问。
清单式的质疑把对话变成审问，他会转成防守。
假顾虑一听就是套话，反而削弱后面所有回答的可信度。
带上假设，他只需要确认或纠正，回答成本很低。
optionDirectness_en: Only harmless if you've already decided not to go; otherwise it wastes the opening.
A checklist of doubts turns the exchange into an interrogation and he goes defensive.
A fake concern is obviously a stock line and undercuts everything you said before.
With a hypothesis attached he only has to confirm or correct, which is cheap to answer.
optionScenarioImpacts: 顾虑留到 offer 阶段，那时已经没人能替我解答。
他花剩下的时间辩护，我什么也没学到。
他记住一句客套，对我的判断力没有加分。
他会解释真实的质量流程，我拿到最关键的一条信息。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The concern survives to offer stage, when nobody is left to answer it.
He spends the remaining time defending and you learn nothing.
He remembers a stock pleasantry and your judgment gains nothing.
He explains their real quality process and you get the one fact that matters most.

scenario: 你在整理一份跨公司通用的反问清单，要判断哪些问题值得占用现场那两个提问名额。
scenario_en: You're building a cross-company list of questions and deciding which ones deserve the two live slots.
q: 哪些条件让一个反问值得占名额？（多选）
q_en: Which conditions make a question worth one of the slots? (multiple)
options: 只有研究过这家公司、或听过这一轮的内容才问得出来
答案在 JD 或官网首页上找不到
问题越长越显得有深度，最好一次问三件事
答案能改变我要不要继续这个流程的判断
options_en: It could only be asked by someone who researched this company or listened in this round
The answer isn't in the job description or on the homepage
The longer the question the deeper it sounds, ideally packing in three things
The answer could change whether I continue with this process
why: 值得占名额的问题有三条：别人问不出来、答案不在公开材料里、答案能改变我的判断。三件事塞进一个长问题，对方只会挑最好答的那件答。
why_en: A question earns a slot on three counts — nobody else could ask it, the answer isn't public, and the answer could change my decision; packing three asks into one just gets the easiest one answered.
optionMeanings: 问题带有本场对话或本次研究的痕迹。
答案不是公开材料能查到的。
把三个问题合并成一个长句。
答案会影响我继续或退出的决定。
optionMeanings_en: The question carries traces of this call or this research.
The answer can't be looked up in public material.
Three questions merged into one long sentence.
The answer moves my continue-or-stop decision.
optionDirectness: 只有我能问出来的问题，才证明我真的在场。
公开材料能查到的东西，用提问名额去问是浪费。
长问题里对方只挑最容易的一件答，另外两件消失。
改变不了任何决定的问题，本质上是在闲聊。
optionDirectness_en: A question only I could ask is what proves I was actually present.
Anything findable in public material wastes a slot.
In a long question they answer the easiest part and the other two vanish.
A question that changes no decision is small talk with extra steps.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻知道我做了功课、也在听。
拿到只有内部人知道的判断依据。
看似问了三件，实际只拿到一件的答案。
问完我能明确决定要不要走下一轮。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They immediately see that you did the homework and were listening.
You get a basis for judgment only insiders have.
It looks like three questions but yields one answer.
Afterwards you can decide whether to take the next round.
